abstract: Snf1 is a conserved protein kinase that is required in yeasts for adaptation to nutrient limitation and to utilize alternative carbon sources other than glucose. Previous reports suggested that, unlike other fungi, this kinase could be essential in the methylotrophic yeast Komagataella phaffii. We show here that cells lacking Snf1 are viable, although with impaired growth in 2% glucose or glycerol. Growth is further compromised in low glucose (0.05%) and abolished entirely on methanol. Transcriptomic analysis of cells growing on glucose, glycerol or methanol reveals as a common trait for the snf1 mutation, irrespectively of the carbon source, the induction of genes required for oxidative stress response and cell wall remodeling, as well as drastic repression of ribosomal genes. These alterations likely explain the severe growth defect of the mutant even under glucose-rich conditions. Both phenotypic and transcriptomic data highlight more drastic effects for the snf1 mutation than previously reported for the regulatory gal83 mutant. Expression in S. cerevisiae snf1 cells of both native KpSnf1 and KpSnf1-H, a version carrying the characteristic N-terminal poly-His track of S. cerevisiae Snf1, restored normal growth on low glucose, glycerol or raffinose, but not on ethanol. Both kinases are phosphorylated in response to shift to low glucose or ethanol and they can restore induction of HXT2 in response to a shift to raffinose but fail to induce ADH2 in response to a shift to ethanol, which could explain the inability to restore normal growth on ethanol of the Snf1-deficient S. cerevisiae strain.

summary: Snf1 kinase deletion in Komagataella phaffii is viable but impairs growth on glucose, glycerol and methanol, with altered stress and ribosomal gene expression.
title: The Snf1 protein kinase is not essential in Komagataella phaffii but is required for cell fitness on multiple carbon sources.
